quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of the lane when it is wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: What is one benefit of doing regular maintenance on your motorcycle?

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can help you avoid parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: If you maintain your motorcycle regularly, it will continue to ride like new. Make routine maintenance checks part of your regular care.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle with a sidecar?

options.text: On the motorcycle seat or in the sidecar.
Neither on the seat nor in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps you be seen in any condition. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothing at all times.

questions.question: Which item provides the best protection for a rider?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide the same protection.

questions.question: Can cold tablets affect your ability to ride safely?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your riding ability.
No, they usually do not affect your riding ability.
No, because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your riding ability.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn the side effects of any drug before you take it and ride.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding in Oregon?

options.text: Up to a judge to decide.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has strict penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position improves safety. It keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid hazards, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers do not try to share your lane.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They inform drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, tightening it may fix the problem. If tightening does not work, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Move to the edge of the road
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: When riding on slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: Curved mirrors make cars look:
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors, but they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: At the front of the group
At the back of the group

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back of the group.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while turning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: Entering a turn at too high a speed can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot
You may block the driver's view
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in its blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane
In the right portion of the lane
In any portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves arms exposed
Shoes that stop below the ankle

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Wear tall, sturdy boots that cover your ankles. Choose boots with low heels that will not catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: Goggles can:

options.text: Protect your face but not your eyes
Protect your eyes but not your face
Not protect your face or eyes

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes but not your face
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield protects your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator stop other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding in the left portion of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to leave no large spaces on either side. This reduces space and discourages drivers from trying to share your lane.
